articles.excerpt: Prediction markets give Democrats a 90% chance of taking the House on November 3. For India, a Democratic chamber would mean oversight hearings on tariffs and the H-1B fee rather than quick relief — leverage on money, not veto-proof lawmaking.

articles.nri_angle: The election decides who controls oversight of the tariff, trade and visa policies that fall most heavily on Indian professionals and exporters.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ocasio-Cortez Transfers $1 Million to El-Sayed in Michigan Senate Race's Final Sprint
articles.excerpt: The New York congresswoman campaigned through Michigan's Republican-leaning Upper Peninsula as both parties pour resources into the open seat that may decide control of the Senate.
articles.image_caption: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, who transferred $1 million to a political account backing Abdul El-Sayed's Michigan Senate campaign.

sources.label: The New York Times via Political Wire

articles.nri_angle: The Michigan race runs through metro Detroit's large Arab American and South Asian communities and tests whether an immigrant-background nominee can carry a swing-state Senate ticket.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Democrats Spend $163 Million Making Trump the Face of the Midterms
articles.excerpt: Democratic ads mentioning the president have aired nearly 180,000 times since September 1, while Republicans have spent just $11 million on ads naming their own leader, an AP analysis found.
articles.nri_angle: Which party controls Congress after November 3 shapes immigration enforcement and visa policy debates that directly affect Indian American families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Colorado Child's Flu Death, the Season's First, Renews Vaccination Push
articles.excerpt: The elementary-aged child had no record of a flu shot. Last season killed eight Colorado children, and barely one in ten residents is vaccinated as this season starts early.
articles.image_caption: A flu vaccination. Colorado health officials renewed their vaccination push after the state's first child flu death of the season.

sources.label: Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment

articles.nri_angle: With multigenerational Diwali and holiday gatherings ahead, officials urge families to vaccinate children now — the season's first death came in October, not mid-winter.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian American Cancer Researcher Rachna Shroff Dies at 47 After Terminal Diagnosis
articles.excerpt: University of Arizona oncologist Rachna Shroff, a leading voice on pancreatic and bile duct cancers, died October 11 at 47, weeks after completing a $1.35 million endowment to fund young cancer researchers.
articles.image_caption: Dr. Rachna Shroff in an undated photo. Shroff, a University of Arizona oncologist who led bile duct cancer trials, died on October 11 at age 47.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian American physician-scientist whose career and endowed award directly affect diaspora families facing gastrointestinal cancers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Poland Scrambles Fighter Jets as Russian Strikes Hit Western Ukraine
articles.excerpt: Poland reported no airspace violation after scrambling jets during overnight strikes that cut power to 370,000 people in Volyn, as Bulgaria asked NATO for aircraft and anti-drone systems.
articles.nri_angle: Russian strikes near the Polish border and Bulgaria's request for NATO aircraft show the war's spillover risk for Europe, watched closely by Indian students and workers in the region.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Netflix Replaces Content Chief Bela Bajaria With Former Disney Executive Peter Rice
articles.excerpt: Bajaria leaves after nearly a decade overseeing Bridgerton, Squid Game and Netflix's live-events push, as the streamer cuts about 1,000 jobs and faces slowing engagement growth.
articles.image_caption: Peter Rice, the former Disney executive Netflix is bringing in to replace content chief Bela Bajaria.
articles.nri_angle: Bajaria was one of the most prominent Indian-origin executives in Hollywood, and her push into international and local-language content shaped what diaspora audiences watch on Netflix.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chicago Man Charged With Killing Estranged Wife, Arrested at O'Hare While Fleeing to India
articles.excerpt: Prosecutors say Ankur Patel, 31, lured his estranged wife to Chicago with a promise she could see their daughter — after secretly sending the child to India — then tried to board a flight out of O'Hare.
articles.image_caption: An apartment hallway with a set of keys on the floor. Prosecutors told a Cook County court that Ankur Patel's estranged wife was found dead inside a Chicago apartment in August.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-origin Chicago man faces a first-degree murder charge in the death of his estranged wife, with the couple's five-year-old daughter now in India with his parents.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ukraine Runs Out of Patriot Interceptors as Russian Ballistic Strikes Intensify
articles.excerpt: Kyiv's Patriot stocks are exhausted after the latest strike on its power grid, leaving ballistic missiles largely unintercepted and resupply in doubt amid a clash with Washington.
articles.nri_angle: A global security development with no direct diaspora action; it affects energy prices and allied defence stocks watched by readers worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indians Form Britain's Largest Foreign Workforce as Migrants Take Most New Jobs
articles.excerpt: A Centre for Social Justice report found only 734,000 of 3.7 million additional UK payroll jobs since 2014 went to British nationals, while HMRC data shows Indian nationals held 1,029,300 jobs in December 2025 — more than any other foreign nationality.
articles.nri_angle: With just over one million payroll jobs, Indians are Britain's largest foreign workforce — and the group most exposed if the jobs-and-welfare debate produces tighter settlement rules.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Army Warns Next War Could Reach US Soil Before Deployment
articles.excerpt: Acting chief Gen. Christopher LaNeve says power projection against China would be contested at home, as the Army rewrites its doctrine for disrupted bases, networks and supply lines.
articles.nri_angle: Homeland-defence planning affects base towns across the US where Indian-American service members, defence workers and their families live.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
